faqs.a: A live viewer renders your SVG code in a preview pane as you type, with a short delay so typing stays smooth. An optimizer, by contrast, focuses on shrinking the file by removing comments and whitespace.
faqs.q: How is this different from an SVG optimizer?

faqs.a: Yes, partially. A <style> block with CSS rules works, because the styles travel with the markup. External stylesheets or fonts referenced by URL are not fetched for security reasons.
faqs.q: Does CSS inside the SVG work in the preview?

faqs.a: The preview updates 250 milliseconds after you stop typing. This debounce prevents the browser from re-rendering on every keystroke, which keeps editing fast.
faqs.q: Why does the preview update slightly after I type?

faqs.a: The zoom is a visual scaling of the preview pane only. It uses CSS transform, so the SVG code and any download stay at the original size.
faqs.q: Does zooming change the downloaded file?

faqs.a: Checkerboard shows transparency accurately, light matches most web pages, and dark helps you check light-colored icons that would be invisible on white.
faqs.q: Which stage background should I use?

svg-editor.formula:
preview delay = 250 ms after the last keystroke
rendered zoom = original size × (zoom ÷ 100)

Example: 120 px SVG at 200% zoom renders at 120 × 2 = 240 px in the pane.
howTo: Type or paste SVG code in the left code pane, or load an .svg file.
Watch the right preview pane render the graphic automatically as you type.
Use the zoom slider to inspect details from 25% to 400%.
Switch the stage background to check transparency or light icons on dark.
Copy the code or download the SVG file when you are happy with it.
keyFacts: A live SVG viewer shows the rendered graphic next to the code that produces it.
The preview refreshes with a 250 ms debounce so fast typing never stutters.
Zoom is a CSS transform on the preview only; it never alters the SVG itself.
A checkerboard stage background reveals transparent areas that white would hide.
The validity indicator turns green only when the code parses as well-formed XML.
Line and character counts help you track file size while you edit.
svg-editor.keywords: svg editor viewer, live svg preview, svg playground, view svg code online

labels.errorInvalid: The SVG code is not valid XML. Fix it before downloading.
labels.errorSvgSize: The SVG file must be smaller than 5 MB.
labels.invalidNote: The code is not valid SVG yet. Fix the markup to see a preview.

limitations: This is for editing and viewing code, not for drawing with a mouse.
Very complex files with thousands of elements can still feel heavy.
External images and fonts referenced by URL are blocked from the preview.
The debounce means the preview always lags typing by a fraction of a second.
